# Incident Report: mta-2026-01-31

## Evidence Reviewed
`2026-01-31-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (51,181 frames, 26.4 MB). No separate IDS/Suricata alert export was present in the evidence directory — this analysis is derived entirely from raw packet data via tshark.

## Victim Host
| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **10.1.21.58** |
| MAC address | **00:21:5d:c8:0e:f2** (Intel NIC) |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-ES9F3ML** (workgroup: WIN11OFFICE) |
| Logged-in Windows user | **gwyatt** (confirmed via Kerberos AS-REQ CNameString) |

Identity confirmed cross-referencing DHCP Discover/Request (option 12 hostname), NBNS name registrations, and Kerberos ticket requests — all three point to the same host/MAC on the LAN.

## Malware Family
**Attribution: behavioral, not signature-confirmed.** No Suricata/IDS alert file was provided, and the actual payload was transferred over TLS (encrypted), so no file hash could be recovered from the wire to confirm a specific family name.

The traffic pattern is consistent with a **fake file-download-portal delivery chain leading to a browser-fingerprinting/gate panel and information-stealer style check-in** — the same TTP pattern documented for Lumma Stealer / Vidar-class loaders distributed via bogus "file share" sites (fake CAPTCHA / TDS-gated delivery). This should be treated as an unconfirmed stealer/loader infection pending sandbox detonation or EDR telemetry, not as a confirmed named family.

## Attack Timeline (all times UTC+4, capture date 2026-01-28)
1. **03:04:49.22** — DNS query to `hiyter.com` (initial lure/redirector)
2. **03:04:49.76** — DNS query to `media.megafilehub4.lat` (fake file-host landing page)
3. **03:04:52.19** — DNS query to `arch.filemegahab4.sbs`; immediately followed by a **16 MB** TLS download from `104.21.46.67:443` (session 10.1.21.58:54840↔104.21.46.67:443, 22.4s duration) — this is almost certainly the malware archive/payload retrieval
4. **~42s gap** (payload likely extracted/executed by the user)
5. **03:05:34** — DNS to `whooptm.cyou`
6. **03:05:36–03:05:47** — Repeated HTTP(S) sessions to `whitepepper.su` (153.92.1.49), including a full browser-fingerprint collection (WebGL, canvas, audio, WebRTC, screen, hardware) POSTed to `/api/set_agent`, run once impersonating Chrome and once impersonating Edge
7. **03:06:06** — DNS to `holiday-forever.cc`
8. **03:06:10** — DNS to `communicationfirewall-security.cc`

## Indicators of Compromise

**Malicious domains**
- `hiyter.com`
- `media.megafilehub4.lat`
- `arch.filemegahab4.sbs`
- `whooptm.cyou`
- `whitepepper.su`
- `holiday-forever.cc`
- `communicationfirewall-security.cc`

**C2 / gate endpoints (IP:port)**
- `153.92.1.49:80` and `153.92.1.49:443` — whitepepper.su, fingerprint-collection/C2 panel
- `104.21.46.67:443` — arch.filemegahab4.sbs, payload delivery (Cloudflare-fronted, ECH-encrypted SNI)
- `104.21.48.156:443` — media.megafilehub4.lat
- `104.21.9.36:443` — communicationfirewall-security.cc
- `80.97.160.24:443` — holiday-forever.cc
- `62.72.32.156:443` — whooptm.cyou
- `104.21.22.231:443` — hiyter.com

**Malicious URLs (observed in cleartext HTTP)**
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Chrome`
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Chrome&act=log` (POST, 8023 bytes — fingerprint exfil)
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Edge`
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Edge&act=log` (POST, 7975 bytes — fingerprint exfil)

Bot/victim ID observed in the panel: `3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C`, token `842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b`.

**Transferred files / hashes**
No file name or SHA256 hash could be recovered. The only file-sized transfer (16 MB, arch.filemegahab4.sbs → 10.1.21.58:54840) rode entirely over TLS with an ECH-obscured SNI (`cloudflare-ech.com`), so its content is not recoverable from this capture. No plaintext HTTP file transfers of executables, archives, or scripts were observed. All non-encrypted objects present in the capture (favicon.ico, connecttest.txt, the whitepepper.su fingerprinting HTML/JS page) are supporting infrastructure, not the payload itself.

## Assessment
The host DESKTOP-ES9F3ML (10.1.21.58, user gwyatt) accessed a fake file-download portal chain (hiyter.com → megafilehub4.lat → filemegahab4.sbs), pulled a 16 MB encrypted payload, and shortly after began communicating with a browser-fingerprinting/tracking panel (whitepepper.su) plus several short-lived gate domains (whooptm.cyou, holiday-forever.cc, communicationfirewall-security.cc). This is consistent with a stealer/loader infection chain, but confirmation of the specific malware family requires either a memory/disk forensic acquisition of the host or a Suricata/YARA match against the actual binary, neither of which is available in this evidence set.
